page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-192GB is an x86_64 architecture cloud server belonging to the Cloud Native family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, powered by AMD EPYC 7542 processors operating at 2.0 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities but weak single-core execution. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 746.4, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak at 8.84 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics are more robust, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 11309.02 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8193.0, both placing in the middle 50%. Memory performance shows a similar divergence: while uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are average at 102.97 GB/sec and 74.72 GB/sec respectively, the PassMark memory score is weak, falling in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM text generation is highly constrained, with the 70B model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10% at 4.46 tokens/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the high memory density of 12.0 GB per core, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated single-core CPU performance. The high memory capacity relative to compute resources makes it suitable for large-scale caching, in-memory database operations, and multi-threaded data processing. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks, real-time text generation, or workloads requiring dedicated CPU pinning.
